Use case: ui-mockup. Create one realistic production-quality FrameIQ desktop video-frame-extraction UI concept, 1440 x 960 landscape proportions, high resolution, app content only, flat straight-on screenshot, no laptop/device bezel, perspective, mockup board, external caption or watermark.
Reference roles: first reference is the existing FrameIQ screenshot REJECTED by the user. It supplies implemented controls and behavior ONLY, not an approved composition; replace its layout completely, do not reproduce huge dead space/small central test-pattern image. Second and third references are actual inspected editable DesignCode dark glass menu/button components, STYLE REFERENCES. Reuse their translucent charcoal/navy surfaces, fine edge highlights, layered soft offset shadows and sober line icons. Adapt for actual FrameIQ functions; do not copy Account/Pricing/Billing/Support/Contact menu labels.
Use Inter typography. Dark navy #060715, white foreground, 70% white secondary text, action blue #3395FF with dark navy text for readable contrast, subtle purple #7147FF and cyan #42E8FF light outside the image. Panel radii10px, controls8px. Glass is functional chrome, not a blur overlay over content. Image canvas opaque neutral charcoal. Crisp readable14px labels, precise timestamp numerals. Refined professional creative tool, not sci-fi HUD or sales website.
Focus primary workflow: exact frame selection, then export. Keep image prominent, timeline thumbnail scrubber, small precise previous/play/next controls, timestamp entry, selected frame thumbnails and one clear 'Select frame' action; include 'Import video', 'Export', Projects and Settings access. Frame details may be shown sparingly: '1920 × 1080', 'Frame 128', '00:00:05.333'. No AI, shopping, fake analytics or dashboards.
Use the SAME plausible source scene for this ideation set: a fully clothed adult woman in a cream blouse, dark navy wide-leg trousers and black shoes, in a real softly lit fashion studio, full-body fashion inspection frame with neutral gray background. Filmstrip shows different moments/poses from this same shot. Selected thumbnails correspond to the source. Imagery is illustrative mock video, not test bars. Image should occupy most of its allocated area without stretching, distortion or clipping the outfit.
Straight utility copy ONLY: 'FrameIQ', 'Studio', 'Projects', 'Import video', 'Select frame', 'Export', 'Selected frames', 'Frame details', 'outfit-study.mp4'. No slogans, promotional headlines, local-processing shields/badges or 'Find your best frame'. No subscription/account/billing. Intentional spacing/grouping and restrained dividers; do not nest cards within cards or fill screen with arbitrary panels/feature inventory. All content fit naturally and controls remain legible.
Current date2026-10-08, do not include dates, prices or time-sensitive data.

Direction name: Focus rail. A fresh asymmetric editing studio. Narrow compact top bar with FrameIQ and source dropdown, Projects icon, Import video and Settings. Large high-resolution video viewport occupies left ~78% width and almost all workspace height, showing source frame large. A slim floating tool cluster hugs the lower-left edge of the viewer, not centered beneath a tiny image. A single glass right rail ~260px wide is dedicated to selected frames: three substantial portrait thumbnails in a vertical column with compact timestamps, counter and Export action at the bottom. Below the main viewer only, a neatly integrated horizontal filmstrip and fine timeline fill left width, with playhead and time marks. Playback/frame stepping and timestamp are a compact horizontal control strip above the filmstrip. Metadata is a small floating popover in the viewer's upper-right, not a permanent dense inspector. Deliberate asymmetry, strongest emphasis on an oversized image, concise chrome, cool indigo illumination on right collection rail. No permanent navigation sidebar. All elements visually coordinated using the attached DesignCode glass/button patterns. Do not show the direction name in the app.

Direction name: Open stage. A substantially different cinema-first canvas composition. Remove all side rails and heavy surrounding frames. A very thin top command row at screen edges: FrameIQ left, 'outfit-study.mp4' next to it; Projects, Import video, Settings right. One huge edge-to-edge central photographic video stage across the full app width from just below header to about65% screen height, opaque neutral charcoal/gray, image fully legible, full-body fashion source fitted. Tool controls are a single short glass bar ABOVE the viewer just below header, grouped toward center (previous, play, next, timestamp '00:00:05.333', Select frame). Small zoom/reset icons are pinned near upper right of stage. A slim integrated thumbnail timeline is directly below the image, only about80px tall, with a precise blue playhead and time ticks rather than a large boxed timeline. The bottom ~180px is a horizontally arranged selected-frame shelf on an open navy surface, three broad image thumbnails side by side left, source/time text beneath, 'Selected frames 3' above, Export action far right. No permanent sidebar and no fixed inspector; only a small 'Frame details' toggle. Use fewer visible borders, generous aligned whitespace, expressive indigo/cyan lighting near outer lower edges. Main image is visually expansive, no excessive wasted dark canvas. Premium unobtrusive controls adapted from attached DesignCode components. A single cohesive application surface rather than stacked boxes; materially different from right-rail layouts and centered floating docks. Do not show the direction name in the app.

Direction name: Precision workbench. A distinct comparison-oriented editing desk. Two large image panes side by side occupy most of the workspace: left labeled 'Current frame', right labeled 'Selected frame'. Current frame shows front view of the full outfit; selected frame shows a side view of the same adult woman and outfit, illustrating manual visual inspection of two frames, not AI. Both panes opaque neutral gray with images clean and unstretched, no floating controls covering the subject. One narrow glass header has FrameIQ / Projects left, source 'outfit-study.mp4' centered, Import video and Settings right. Immediately beneath header a purposeful slim tools row: previous/play/next, editable timestamp '00:00:05.333', 'Frame 128', prominent Select frame left; zoom100% and Frame details on right. Current pane subtly edged in cyan, selected pane a tiny selected-frame timestamp label, separators subtle. Below both large panes a single full-width navy timeline deck: fine timestamp ruler and blue playhead above a filmstrip of thumbnail frames; a compact precision-wheel tick track aligned with transport rather than huge blank box. Along the very bottom, a 64px high unobtrusive collection strip 'Selected frames 3' with three small source thumbnails/timestamps and Export blue action right. Use authentic DesignCode dark-glass button/tab styling with blue/purple/cyan peripheral illumination, grounded cohesive creative-tool layout. No permanent side rail, no giant dock overlapping photograph, no marketing. Strong horizontally organized comparison workflow, visibly unlike single image right-collection layout and full-width open-stage layouts. Any comparison content is an illustrative UI concept, no invented matching scores. Do not show the direction name in the app.
